summary.text: Rory Lancman is the Democratic candidate for New York State Senate District 7 in the November 3, 2026 general election, an open seat with no incumbent.
An attorney, he served in the New York State Assembly from 2007 to 2013 and on the New York City Council from 2013 to 2020.

paragraphs.text: Rory Lancman earned a bachelor's degree from Queens College, City University of New York, and a J.D. from Columbia Law School.

He worked as counsel for Pensterstock & Partners, LLP and as an associate with Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson, and he served as a first lieutenant in the New York Army National Guard infantry.

Lancman represented District 25 in the New York State Assembly from 2007 to 2013, and during the 2011-2012 session his committee assignments included Banks, Cities, Codes, Housing, Judiciary and Labor, with a chair role on the Subcommittee on Workplace Safety.
He ran unsuccessfully for the U.S. House in 2012, losing the Democratic primary in New York's 6th Congressional District to Grace Meng.
He then served on the New York City Council, representing District 24 from 2013 until November 2, 2020, and he ran in the 2019 Democratic primary for Queens County District Attorney.
